title: Feedback on usage
body:
Hi all, 

I was considering using Triton for my class, but after using it for a day, I've run into a lot of issues. I think the library probably needs a more of a warning note on the front page, so others don't run into issues in practice. 

If you are considering using triton, be aware of these problems.

* Use of broadcasting dimension such as `a[None, :]` often yields strange llvm errors. had to replace these with views or different loading.
* Using dimensions greater than 2 often leads to strange llvm errors without line number outputs. 
* Often there are no line number errors at all. I get things like `AttributeError: 'Slice' object has no attribute 'lineno'`
* Many fail or produce strange errors. For instance `tl.trans` seems to not be supported at all. Operators like `device_print` seem not to exist.
* Operators that are supported like `tl.dot` have undocumented constraints on their sizes. 
* Certain sequences of operations like broadcast followed by sum seem to fail. Have to get around these by reordering ops. 
* Non-standard use of view. Does not behave in a Pytorch compatible yielding confusing output. Is silent though and will happily output random views.  

Triton seems like the future, and the promise of having an array like language to do CUDA programming is amazing. However, I think the v2.0 made me think it was a bit further along in usability. Just be aware that there are  many sharp bits 🔪 🔪 🔪 🔪

comments.body:
Interesting, I'm also using triton in my class, :)

We can chat more about it experience :)

- Use of broadcasting dimension such as a[None, :] often yields strange llvm errors. had to replace these with views or different loading.

If you are referring to 3d cases, that would be something we don't have good support yet. Otherwise, can you please submit a specific example?

- Often there are no line number errors at all. I get things like AttributeError: 'Slice' object has no attribute 'lineno'

Again, I'm interested in the specific example.

- Many fail or produce strange errors. For instance tl.trans seems to not be supported at all. Operators like device_print seem not to exist.

`tl.trans` has certain constraints. WDM `device_print` doesn't exist? Are you using triton/main?

- Operators that are supported like tl.dot have undocumented constraints on their sizes.

They have been documented in the code.

- Non-standard use of view. Does not behave in a Pytorch compatible yielding confusing output. Is silent though and will happily output random views.

We are aware of the constraints of the view operation, along with `tl.cat` that suffers from similar issues. No immediate plan to improve it though.
